title: Workload migration comparison: on-premises to cloud

slides.purpose: Set up the one decision the story answers.
slides.takeaway: Should this workload move to the cloud?

blocks.label: Evidence, not hype
blocks.body: Follow one workload from fixed capacity to a reversible pilot.

slides.notes: The same small co-presenter continues through all five slides.

scene.staticDescription: One IT admin enters through a doorway and considers where the workload should run.

cues.semantic: The same admin enters, looks around and thinks before choosing a platform

slides.takeaway: Fixed capacity is bought for the peak, so most of it sits idle

blocks.label: Patching, power and spares stay with you

scene.staticDescription: An IT admin racks servers sized for the busiest hour. A load meter beside the rack shows a brief peak and an average near 18% (illustrative). The admin shrugs, then checks the time spent on upkeep.

cues.semantic: Admin racks servers; the load meter peaks once, then idles near 18% while upkeep chores pile up

slides.notes: The 18% figure is illustrative. Point at the gap between the peak line and the average.

slides.purpose: Show elastic capacity and its honest costs.
slides.takeaway: Cloud capacity can follow demand, but it is not automatically cheaper

blocks.label: Capacity scales up and down with demand
Egress and always-on use still cost money

scene.staticDescription: The admin has an idea: a cloud whose capacity bars rise and fall with the demand line. The admin presents it, then stops to think about migration effort and running costs.

cues.semantic: Capacity bars follow the demand line; cost tags appear while the admin weighs trade-offs

slides.notes: Elastic does not mean cheap: steady, always-on workloads and data egress can cost more.

slides.purpose: Turn the comparison into a short evidence process.
slides.takeaway: Build the evidence before moving anything

scene.staticDescription: The admin follows Measure, Validate, Compare cost and Pilot; each step produces evidence.

cues.semantic: The admin moves along the four steps while each one lights up

slides.notes: Every step produces data for the decision; the pilot is time-boxed and reversible.

slides.purpose: Close with a clear, balanced recommendation.
slides.takeaway: Move what fits; retain what does not

blocks.label: Move
blocks.body: Spiky or growing demand, proven by the pilot.

blocks.label: Retain
blocks.body: Steady or constrained demand; lower cost on-premises.

blocks.label: Next step
blocks.body: One workload. A time-boxed pilot. Then decide.

slides.notes: End on the action: one workload, one pilot, then decide.

scene.staticDescription: After a successful pilot, the admin celebrates with a basketball shot, then leaves through the doorway.

cues.semantic: Celebrate a successful pilot, not indiscriminate migration; then leave through the door

blocks.label: Move
blocks.body: Spiky or growing workloads the pilot shows run well in the cloud.

blocks.label: Retain
blocks.body: Steady, latency-bound or regulated workloads that cost less where they are.

blocks.label: Next step
blocks.body: Pick one workload and run a time-boxed pilot.
